summary: Good CGM coverage and strong overall time in range, but with meaningful hypoglycemia exposure, a recurring late-morning to afternoon rise, and no logged carbohydrate data. The package does not support a supported change to basal, CR, ISF, target, or AAPS automation yet; the safest sequence is to keep current settings, collect meal-linked evidence, and reassess one parameter family at a time.

analysis_steps.findings: CGM and telemetry quality are strong enough for review: 3995 CGM entries over 14 days, 98.7% coverage, no invalid or duplicate entries, and only 10 gaps with the largest 65 minutes. The profile context is clear because the top-level aaps_profile is authoritative. The main limitation is the absence of carb treatment entries, which prevents clean meal-versus-basal separation.
data_gaps: No meal timing or composition data
Some windows overlap with temporary targets and device events

analysis_steps.findings: Overall control is strong, but hypoglycemia is not trivial and variability is elevated. Time below range is 5.1% with lows into the low 40s mg/dL, while time above range is 8.9% and CV is 32.6%. The pattern requires conservative interpretation because both low and high exposure coexist.
data_gaps: Some lows and highs coincide with corrections, temporary targets, and device events

analysis_steps.findings: The target schedule is plausible and not obviously inconsistent with the observed data. The strongest local pattern is higher glucose from about 10:00 to 17:00, while overnight and late-evening windows show more low exposure. However, the daytime rise is confounded by likely meal and correction effects, so no isolated basal defect is proven.
evidence: targets 90 mg/dL at 00:00 and 23:00, 100 mg/dL at 08:00
local hourly averages highest from 10:00 to 17:00
local lows cluster around 00:00 to 01:00 and 22:00 to 23:00
data_gaps: Overnight and daytime patterns are both confounded by corrections and temporary targets

analysis_steps.findings: The CR schedule suggests stronger insulin need in the 04:00 and 16:00 segments than at other times, but the dataset does not isolate whether that reflects meal timing, bolus timing, or true ratio mismatch. ISF and DIA are plausible and not clearly broken. The correction windows are sparse and noisy, so no supported CR, ISF, or DIA change is justified from this period alone.
evidence: CR segments vary from 10.5 to 13.2 g/U
correction windows include both large drops and rebounds
no carb entries are available to match meals to responses
data_gaps: No declared per-meal prebolus or immediate bolus values in the package
No separate insulin-action test free of meal and target confounding

analysis_steps.findings: SMB and UAM are enabled in a coherent way and appear to function as a correction backstop rather than a duplicate COB counter. The configuration does not show a material inconsistency. Because meal data are absent, SMB/UAM activity cannot be cleanly separated from meal absorption, but there is no evidence that the mode itself is the primary problem.
evidence: representative loop logs show SMB use during rising glucose
data_gaps: No direct test of SMB behavior without meal confounding
Temporary targets and device events overlap with key excursions

analysis_steps.findings: Autosens is disabled while dynamic sensitivity is enabled, which is not a contradiction. A sensitivity_ratio of 1 in loop output is neutral and does not mean the feature is disabled. The max basal and max IOB limits are not obviously constraining routine operation, and there is no evidence that changing automation limits would be safer than first resolving the profile and meal ambiguity.
evidence: representative sensitivity_ratio values around 1 are neutral
data_gaps: No evidence that current safety ceilings are the bottleneck
Hypoglycemia risk limits any move toward stronger automation

analysis_steps.findings: The package does not provide a declared stable meal strategy to reproduce, and carb treatment entries are absent. The observed pattern suggests that meal timing may matter, especially in the late morning to afternoon, but the data do not support a specific prebolus or immediate bolus percentage. SMB/UAM should remain the correction backstop rather than a substitute for meal coverage.
evidence: local hourly glucose is highest from about 10:00 to 17:00
low exposure is present overnight and after some corrections
data_gaps: No bolus timing relative to meals
No per-meal confirmation of declared strategy

analysis_steps.findings: There is no evidence supporting a routine e-carb strategy in this period. No carb entries, no extended carb entries, and no e-carb duration are available. The 6-hour responses are too confounded by corrections, temp basals, IOB, temporary targets, and device events to infer e-carb need or absorption behavior.
evidence: no meal-linked carb records are present
data_gaps: No way to separate meal absorption from correction and automation effects

analysis_steps.findings: The contradiction audit does not support changing any dependent settings together. The safest coherent interpretation is: keep the current profile and automation settings, because the daytime highs and overnight/late-evening lows are both real but remain confounded by missing meal data, corrections, temporary targets, and device events. The current system is internally coherent, and the data are not clean enough to justify a supported basal, CR, ISF, target, SMB, UAM, or e-carb change.
evidence: time below range 5.1% with lows in the low 40s mg/dL
no carb entries or meal strategy declaration

strengths.title: High-quality CGM coverage
strengths.description: Coverage is 98.7% with no invalid or duplicate entries, so broad time-of-day pattern review is reliable.

strengths.title: Overall glycemic control is strong
strengths.description: Average glucose is 121.6 mg/dL and TIR is 86%, which is good despite variability and isolated lows.

strengths.title: Automation configuration is internally coherent
strengths.description: SMB, UAM, dynamic sensitivity, and safety ceilings are consistent with closed-loop use and do not show an obvious setup conflict.

issues.title: Meaningful hypoglycemia exposure
issues.description: Time below range is 5.1%, with lows into the low 40s mg/dL, so any move toward more aggressive insulin delivery would need caution.

issues.title: Daytime hyperglycemia cluster
issues.description: Local glucose averages are highest from about 10:00 to 17:00, but the period is confounded by missing carb logs, corrections, and device events.

issues.title: No logged carbohydrate treatments
issues.description: The absence of carb entries prevents clean separation of meal, basal, and automation effects.

recommendations.title: Keep the current profile unchanged and verify with meal-linked observation
recommendations.description: The data do not isolate a basal, CR, ISF, target, or DIA defect. Because both low exposure and daytime highs coexist, and meal data are absent, changing any dependent setting now would be unsupported.

suggested_change.sequence: hold basal, CR, ISF, target, and automation settings steady
suggested_change.verification: record one or two meals with exact carb amount and bolus timing, then compare the next 6 hours of CGM before revisiting any profile edit

profile_recommendation.recommendation: Keep the current basal profile unchanged for now; verify one overnight window and one late-morning meal window with exact carb logging before considering any basal change.
profile_recommendation.rationale: Basal is the most plausible future review area because overnight lows and daytime highs both exist, but the period is too confounded by missing meal logs, corrections, temporary targets, and device events to justify a supported change now.
profile_recommendation.next_check: Log one overnight and one midday meal with exact carbs and bolus timing, then compare the 6-hour CGM response before changing basal.

parameter_decisions.rationale: Overnight lows are present, but they overlap with IOB, correction timing, and several safe overnight windows. The evidence does not isolate this segment as the cause, and changing it now could worsen low exposure without proving benefit.
The early-morning period is not clearly separable from dawn-like rises, meal timing, or residual IOB. There is no supported basis to change this basal without a cleaner fasting window.

Morning glucose rises exist later in the day, but they are more compatible with meal timing or bolus timing than with an isolated 06:00 basal fault. No supported change is separable from meal effects.
The strongest daytime highs occur after this time, but meal data are absent and SMB/UAM plus corrections are active. The evidence is insufficient to call this basal too low.

This lower late-day basal may be helping limit lows, and the data do not separate its effect from meal and correction patterns. Given the low exposure, increasing aggressiveness here would be unsupported.
Late-evening lows exist, but they are confounded by IOB and correction effects. No isolated basal change is justified.
The evening window shows mixed behavior rather than a clean basal defect. The safer action is to keep this unchanged until meal-linked evidence is available.
There is no meal log to test this ratio, and the overnight period includes low exposure rather than a clear meal-driven requirement. A change would be speculative.
This ratio could be relevant if early-morning meals are present, but there is no meal-linked evidence to support change. The correction and IOB data are too sparse to isolate it.
Late-morning highs may reflect lunch timing rather than this CR segment, and no carb entries are available. The evidence is insufficient for a supported change.
This segment is the most plausible meal-related candidate, but the absence of meal logs prevents confirming undercoverage versus timing effects. Keep until meal-linked data are available.
Evening lows and overnight lows are more prominent than a consistent evening meal-rise pattern. With no carb data, a CR change is unsupported.
Correction responses are mixed and heavily confounded by IOB, temporary targets, and device events. The data do not support a reliable ISF change.
The current target is consistent with the observed overnight profile and there is no evidence that target changes would solve the mixed low/high pattern better than meal-linked review.
The daytime rise is not clearly target-driven because the highs are more likely meal- or correction-related and the data include low exposure. No supported target change is present.
Late-evening and overnight lows argue against making the target more aggressive. The current target is already conservative enough for this dataset.
The DIA is plausible for this loop setup and is not clearly the driver of the mixed response windows. There is no evidence that changing DIA would be safer than resolving meal timing first.
The SMB/UAM system is coherent and not shown to be a material fault. It likely acts as a correction backstop in the presence of meal uncertainty, so changing it now would be unsupported.
The activation rules are internally consistent. No material conflict or safety issue is visible, and the dataset does not prove that these rules are the source of the highs or lows.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS / max basal and max IOB limits
parameter_decisions.rationale: These ceilings are not obviously constraining routine action in the supplied telemetry. Because the period includes lows into the low 40s mg/dL, making the system more aggressive would not be supported.
This configuration is internally consistent. A sensitivity_ratio of 1 is neutral rather than disabled. The data do not justify changing sensitivity settings before meal-linked evidence is available.
There are no carb entries or extended-carb entries to validate this model against. The 6-hour responses are too confounded to support any change.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Keep prebolus conservative, do not assign a routine immediate-bolus percentage from this dataset, leave SMB/UAM as the correction backstop, and do not add routine e-carbs without meal-linked evidence.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: The package shows no logged carb treatments, no stable declared meal-strategy values, and mixed correction responses through 6 hours. The strongest recurring pattern is a late-morning to afternoon rise, but that is confounded by missing meal logs, IOB, temp targets, and device events. Low exposure into the low 40s mg/dL means any more aggressive meal timing would need much stronger evidence.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Record one meal with exact carb amount and bolus timing, then observe the next 6 hours of CGM while keeping other settings unchanged.

exceptions.suggestion: If this rise repeats after the same meal, review meal timing before changing basal or automation.
exceptions.rationale: Local glucose is highest from about 10:00 to 17:00, but the package cannot separate meal timing from correction and automation effects.

exceptions.suggestion: Avoid routine prebolus when starting near the low end or after recent insulin.
exceptions.rationale: Overnight and some late-day lows, including values in the low 40s mg/dL, make aggressive prebolus timing risky in this dataset.

education: A sensitivity_ratio of 1 is a neutral adjustment, not proof that dynamic sensitivity is disabled.
SMB waiting-time messages do not mean the configured SMB interval has changed.
Missing carb logs do not prove missed insulin; they only limit the ability to separate meal effects from profile or automation effects.
safety_notes: This is decision-support content only; independently verify every proposed change.
Make changes one at a time and monitor glucose closely after each change.
Because lows reached the low 40s mg/dL, avoid making the system more aggressive without meal-linked evidence.
Do not change dependent insulin-delivery settings together when the same pattern could be explained by meal timing, IOB, correction timing, or temporary targets.
